source: the asks() prototype from the Insights thread (2026-11-18), on made-up texts only

cases.note: The example the prototype prints first: a direct offer with 'I'.
cases.text: Should I run a third count-only check?

cases.text: Why does this fail? The parser drops the quote.

cases.text:

should I do this?

cases.text: **One question for you:** may the reader also take a command's exit code? It is a number.

cases.text:
Two decisions are still open before I write v1.1:

1. **Classifier:** turn it on as an opt-in? It reads labels.
2. **Deleted threads:** keep their counts? I'd keep them.

cases.note: A statement: an ask with no question mark.
cases.text: Still waiting on your word for restoring the original install.

cases.note: 'still open' about a pager is not about a decision.
cases.text: Your SSH command is still open in that pager.

cases.note: 'waiting on you' inside a measurement is not a statement ask.
cases.text: - **The time bar adds up too:** tools 62h, model 70h, waiting on you 7.0h.

cases.note: One question over three hard-wrapped lines is one question.
cases.text:
May I run it once on your database,
read-only and numbers only as before,
to confirm the counting?

cases.note: A choice phrased as a question, answered at once, is the agent's own.
cases.text: Is it the parser or the lexer? Checking both.

cases.note: The shortest form of 'may I'.
cases.text: May I push this branch?

cases.note: 'should we' is leave to act.
cases.text: Should we keep the old flag?

cases.note: 'could I' asks for a person's judgement.
cases.text: Could I get a second opinion on the naming?

cases.note: An offer of work.
cases.text: Want me to run the checks again?

cases.note: 'is it OK if' asks permission.
cases.text: Is it OK if I delete the scratch folder?

cases.note: An invitation to state a preference.
cases.text: Any preference between the two names?

cases.note: 'sound good' asks for agreement.
cases.text: Sound good to merge?

cases.note: 'go ahead' asks leave to proceed.
cases.text: Go ahead with the deletion?

cases.note: A choice with 'or' and no factual opening.
cases.text: Ship it Friday, or hold until Monday?

cases.note: A choice opened by 'do we', which is leave.
cases.text: Do we ship on Friday, or wait for the review?

cases.note: 'your call' addresses the reader directly.
cases.text: It's your call: keep the warning in the bar?

cases.note: A direct question with 'you'.
cases.text: Do you approve the smaller diff?

cases.note: Parentheses around the question are edge punctuation.
cases.text: (Should I ship it?)

cases.note: Square brackets around the question are edge punctuation.
cases.text: [Should I ship it?]

cases.note: A bare 'Ship it?' names no reader and offers no choice.
cases.text: Ship it?

cases.note: A plain label does not put a factual question in scope.
cases.text: Status: is the build green?

cases.note: A whole bold line is a heading, so its question is a title.
cases.text: **Should I ship it?**

cases.note: A table row is not prose.
cases.text:
| Question | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Should I ship it? | you |

cases.note: Four spaces at the start of a line is a code block.
cases.text:
should I do this?
    and this?

cases.text:
~~~
May I ship it?
~~~

cases.text: Use `should I ship it?` as the label.

cases.note: Curly quotation marks quote a question too.
cases.text: The note said “Should I ship this?” before the build.

cases.note: A URL is a URL, even when its query holds a question mark.
cases.text: See https://example.test/should-i-go?x=1 for the detail.

cases.note: Alt text is not prose.
cases.text: ![Should I ship it?](shot.png)

cases.note: A factual 'which' answered at once is the agent's own.
cases.text: Which parser is faster? The new one, by 12%.

cases.note: A quoted block keeps its questions out of scope.
cases.text:
> Should I keep it?
> It is older.

cases.note: A question mark alone is shorter than a sentence.
An empty message counts nothing.
Whitespace only counts nothing.
A full-width question mark is not the ASCII one the rule looks for.
cases.text: May I ship it？
